title: Silas and the Ember
premise: When the border wards collapse and the stars go dark, Marguerite Montrose's hidden gift for speaking with beasts becomes the only thing standing between the city of Vell and the starving wilds beyond. Guided by Silas, a scarred ember-dragon who remembers the old covenant between realms, Marguerite must gather the scattered oath-keepers—human, beast, and something stranger—to reforge what their ancestors broke. The price of survival, they learn, is not blood but belonging: someone must willingly give up the life they've built to become the covenant's living anchor. In the end, Marguerite binds herself to the renewed pact, trading her anonymity for a place in both worlds as the stars reignite.
about_author: Orsen Almeida is a former wildlife rehabilitator who spent a decade listening to animals no one else could reach before turning to fiction. They write from a farmhouse at the edge of a national forest, where the boundary between the tame and the wild is a daily negotiation.

chapters.title: Charms for a Godless City
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. We meet them selling luck-knots and mouse-whispers in Vell's night market, hiding their beast-speech behind harmless trinkets while ward-inspectors patrol. A stray cat delivers an impossible message: the wards are failing. Emotional beat: the loneliness of a gift that must stay buried.

chapters.title: The Night the Stars Went Out
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. The border wards shatter; darkness swallows the sky and panic floods the streets. Fleeing the inspectors who finally suspect them, Marguerite escapes through the broken gate into the wilds—and hears, for the first time in years, the land itself speaking. Beat: terror giving way to terrible freedom.

chapters.title: Ash on the Wind
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Lost in the changed wilderness, they follow a trail of warm ash to a cave and find Silas, the last ember-dragon, dying by inches since the covenant broke three centuries ago. He offers a bargain: his fire for her voice. Beat: wary hope kindling between two survivors.

chapters.title: What the Wolves Remember
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV, traveling with Silas disguised as a hound. The wolf-packs guard the first oath-stone but demand a toll: a truth spoken aloud that the speaker has never confessed. Marguerite admits she let her mother be taken by inspectors rather than reveal herself. Beat: grief as payment.

chapters.title: The Cartographer's Daughter
chapters.summary: Isolde's POV. A human cartographer whose family secretly mapped the old covenant sites joins the quest, revealing that Vell's founders deliberately broke the pact to hoard magic for themselves. Isolde struggles with inheriting her father's guilt. Beat: the weight of inheritance.

chapters.title: River of Small Betrayals
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. The party bargains with the river-folk, shape-shifting eel-people who test loyalty by offering each traveler their heart's desire. Isolde nearly accepts a map home; Marguerite refuses a vision of a safe, ordinary life. Beat: temptation and the cost of refusing comfort.

chapters.title: The Hollow King
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. At the mountain forge, they confront the Hollow King—a human lord who consumed the covenant's anchor-stone to rule both realms, and who now starves as its power gutters. He offers Marguerite partnership: share the stone, split the worlds. Beat: the seduction of power over belonging.

chapters.title: Guttering
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. The Hollow King's hunters ambush them; Silas burns nearly to nothing shielding the group, and Isolde is captured. With two stones gathered and one lost, Marguerite must choose between rescuing her friend and reaching the forge before the last dragon-fire dies. Beat: despair at the cliff-edge of sacrifice.

chapters.title: The Reforging
chapters.summary: Climax, Marguerite's POV. At the mountain forge, Marguerite speaks every voice at once—wolf, river, dragon, human—calling all oath-keepers to witness. She offers herself as the living anchor, and Silas gives his final flame not to the stone but to her. The Hollow King, offered belonging he never believed he could have, crumbles. Beat: self-gift as victory.

chapters.title: Stars, Rekindled
chapters.summary: Resolution, alternating POVs. The wards rise again—not walls this time, but doors. Marguerite returns to Vell openly, charms and all, as the first licensed beast-speaker; Silas sleeps beneath the mountain, dreaming warm. Isolde redraws the maps with both realms on one page. Beat: belonging earned, inheritance redeemed.
